# Help Ananya, 7, get the heart surgery she needs
[Image: Photo: Ananya sitting at home with her mother]
Organised by Kavita Rao · Beneficiary: Ananya
## Story
Ananya is a 7-year-old girl from Nashik, Maharashtra. She was born with a hole in her heart (a ventricular septal defect). Her father drives an auto-rickshaw and her mother works as a cook.
Doctors at a hospital in Pune have advised open-heart surgery within the next two months. The surgery, hospital stay and medicines cost ₹3,00,000, which the family cannot pay.
Ananya gets tired quickly and misses some school days. The family has used their savings on tests and check-ups so far.
Every contribution, however small, goes directly to the hospital.
## How the money will be used
| Item | Amount
| Surgery and operating theatre | ₹1,65,000
| ICU and ward stay (10 days) | ₹75,000
| Medicines and tests | ₹45,000
| Follow-up visits for 1 year | ₹15,000
| Total | ₹3,00,000

# Help Fatima restart her tailoring shop and support her children
No photo added by the organiser
Organised by Neha Srivastava · Beneficiary: Fatima
## Story
Fatima is a 34-year-old woman from Lucknow who raises two children alone. She ran a small tailoring shop from home until her sewing machines and stock were sold to pay hospital bills last year.
Two new sewing machines, fabric stock and six months' rent for a small shop cost ₹3,00,000.
Fatima currently earns irregular income from cleaning work. She has a list of former customers who want to order again.
Equipment is bought from a local supplier and the invoice will be posted here.

# Help Priya become the first nurse in her family
[Image: Photo: Priya sitting alone, looking worried, holding her admission letter]
Organised by Sunil Verma · Beneficiary: Priya
## Story
Priya is a 19-year-old young woman from a village near Gaya, Bihar. She scored 86% in Class 12 and has been admitted to a four-year B.Sc. Nursing course. She would be the first person in her family to go to college.
Tuition, hostel and books for the full course cost ₹3,00,000. Her parents are small farmers and cannot pay the fees.
When the admission letter came, Priya cried because she knew the family could not afford it. Her father has already taken a loan after two failed harvests, and she is afraid she will have to give up her dream and stay home.
Fees are paid directly to the college against invoices.
